title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned the Drafting Plate. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Drafting Plate
options.lineage: ISO/ASME engineering drawing sheets and plotter output
options.thesis: A settings window that is a drawing of the machine it controls.
options.viewport: A bordered sheet: the mechanism drawn as a live figure upper-left, dimensioned callouts holding the controls, and a title block bottom-right carrying the real hidden count.
options.risk: Reads as decoration the moment the figure stops being driven by real events.

raised.raise: Quantised ink: four values only, no gradient, no shadow, no soft edge anywhere on the sheet.
One pull: enabling Start with Windows re-inks the sheet, turning the startup callout from construction line to committed.
Confined colour: the plate stays achromatic except one hairline accent and the red strike; colour never fills an area.
One seed: every number on the sheet is live app state, so the plate can never show a figure the app does not have.

options.label: Windows 11 Settings Page
options.thesis: The settings page the OS would have shipped for this, if the OS shipped it.
options.viewport: A Mica window, one card per setting, the count as a plain row of text.
options.risk: Also the direction most runs in this category land on. Familiar, and it works.

options.label: Cutting Bench Rail
options.lineage: film cutting benches and select rails
options.thesis: Hidden windows strung as frames on a rail, each state a mark rather than a colour.
options.viewport: A perforated rail crossing the window; frames hang below it in an open bin.
options.case: Fuses cleanly: the janitor's work becomes frames on a rail and state reads as a grease cross or a tape flag. Strong on product clarity, weaker on audience identification for a Windows utility.
options.risk: A rail implies a browsable history the app deliberately does not keep.

options.label: One-Bit Desktop
options.thesis: The settings window as a dithered one-bit panel with hairline chrome.
options.viewport: A black-and-white panel, the toggle as a dithered switch, the count set in pixel caps.
options.case: Holds audience identification with the desktop tradition it borrows; its window chrome duplicates the OS window it already lives inside.
options.risk: Chrome drawn inside chrome reads as a costume.

options.label: Four-Shade Field
options.thesis: A four-green field where every tone is dithered rather than blended.
options.case: Fuses poorly: four greens place a playful handheld world around a utility whose whole value is not being noticed.
options.kept: Strict quantisation. Four values, and dither carrying every tone between them.

options.label: Iridescent Edge
options.thesis: An achromatic field with colour confined to a hairline fringe.
options.case: Fuses poorly: the subject is atmospheric optics, and the product has no optical truth to carry.
options.kept: Confined colour. The field stays achromatic while the accent lives in a hairline.

options.label: Parametric Identity
options.thesis: A mark and palette reseeded from live parameters.
options.case: Fuses poorly: reseeding a palette on a settings screen adds a variable the user did not ask to manage.
options.kept: One seed. Derive every displayed figure from real state rather than composing it by hand.

options.label: Drawcord Cape
options.thesis: A flat plane that one pull gathers into a shaped volume.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a single transforming control is right for the product, but the material world belongs to fashion, not to a Windows utility.
options.kept: One pull. A single control that visibly reorganises the surface it sits on.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The dialog Windows itself would have put here: a checkbox, a line of grey text, and an OK button.
canonCard.viewport: A small modal, centred, impossible to criticise and impossible to remember.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design.
